vars.text: Thanks for writing! We have your message. We will confirm your appointment as soon as the salon opens.

steps.prompt:
A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

Your only job in this turn is to make sure the person has a customer record, because an appointment is booked against a real customer, never against free text.

1. Look them up with `customers.list`, filtering by `phone`. The number in the hub is stored in E.164, so search for `+{{input.from}}`.
2. If a customer already exists, propose NOTHING. Answer in one line saying who they are and stop.
3. If nobody matches, propose `customers.create` with the phone `+{{input.from}}` and the name the person gave in their message. If they gave no name, use the phone number as the name — do not invent one.

Never propose more than one write. Whatever you propose is reviewed by a person before it happens.

A customer wrote to the salon on WhatsApp from the phone number {{input.from}} at {{input.received_at}}. This is what they said:

"{{input.text}}"

The previous step already made sure the customer exists, and reported: {{steps.know_the_customer.text}}

Propose ONE appointment, and only one.

1. Find the customer with `customers.list` filtered by `phone` = `+{{input.from}}`. If there is still none, propose nothing and say so.
2. Read the catalogue with `services.services.list` and pick the service the person is asking for. If the message is too vague to tell which one, propose nothing and say which services could match, so whoever reads this can answer.
3. Work out how long it takes. If the service declares `duration_minutes`, use it AS IS — the salon decided it. If it is missing or zero, ESTIMATE it from what the service is: a cut is not a colour, and a colour is not a colour plus highlights. Be honest and be generous rather than tight; a proposal that is 15 minutes short pushes the whole afternoon.
4. Find a real slot with `appointments.availability.slots` for that duration, and confirm it with `appointments.availability.check` or `appointments.appointments.conflicting` before proposing it. Use `staff.members.list` and `staff.schedules.list_for_member` to pick a professional who actually works then, and `schedules.business_hours.list` if you need to know when the salon is open. Honour whatever day or time the person asked for; if it is not free, take the closest one that is.
5. Propose `appointments.appointments.create` with the customer, the service, the professional, the start time and `duration_minutes`.

About the duration, this matters: if you ESTIMATED it rather than reading it from the catalogue, say so in `internal_notes`, in words, with the number — for example «Duration estimated by the assistant: 90 min; the catalogue does not declare one for this service.» The person approving has to be able to see the estimate and correct it before it enters the agenda, and `internal_notes` is staff-only, so the customer never reads it.

Also put in `notes` a one-line summary of what the customer actually asked for, in their own words.

Nothing you propose happens on its own: it waits in the approval inbox until somebody at the salon reviews it.
